chunks: And from him, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from a man from our companions who is teknonymed Abu Abdullah, who raised it to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: In opposing the women is the blessing.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.خِلَافِ: Opposition / Not insisting on one's own will / Yielding

ai.seo_question: What does the Shia hadith mean by 'in opposing the women is the blessing'?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) conveys that Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) identified 'opposing the women' (khilaf al-nisa') as a source of blessing. While some interpret this as men yielding to their wives' preferences to maintain harmony, Shia scholars often view it as a strategic humility where the husband, though having authority, chooses to defer to his wife's wishes to avoid conflict, thereby inviting divine barakah into the home.
